title: OU's Biggest Win Over Texas: The 65-13 Red River Rout of 2003
question: What is Oklahoma's largest margin of victory over Texas?
answer: Oklahoma's largest win over Texas is 65-13 on October 11, 2003, in Dallas. The 52-point margin is the biggest in the Red River series, and the 65 points are the most OU has scored against the Longhorns.
summary: OU's 65-13 win over Texas on Oct. 11, 2003, is the largest margin in Red River Rivalry history. Relive the six-turnover, 290-yard passing blowout.
body: Oklahoma's biggest win in the Red River Rivalry came on October 11, 2003, when the top-ranked Sooners beat No. 11 Texas 65-13 at the Cotton Bowl. The 52-point margin topped OU's 63-14 win from three years earlier and stands as the largest in the series.

The Sooners were relentless, scoring two touchdowns in every quarter and taking a 37-13 lead into halftime. Quarterback Jason White completed his first eight throws and finished 17 of 21 for 290 yards and four touchdowns. Receiver Mark Clayton set an OU single-game record with 190 receiving yards.

Bob Stoops' defense was just as dominant. Oklahoma forced six Texas turnovers, including first-quarter interceptions of both Chance Mock and Vince Young, against a Longhorn team that had not thrown an interception all season before that day. Jonathan Jackson added a 21-yard interception return for a touchdown in the second quarter, and Texas never got close.

For the Longhorns, it was the most lopsided loss in what was then a 98-game rivalry. For the Sooners, it was the fourth straight win over Texas, part of a dominant stretch in the series during the early Stoops years.
If a friend at a watch party asks for the record, here is the short version: 65-13 in 2003 is the biggest Sooner win over Texas, and 65 is the most points OU has ever hung on the Longhorns.
